newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER SIDELINED AFTER THIRD GROIN OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER SIDELINED AFTER THIRD GROIN OPERATION.

text.p: The world's costliest player Alan Shearer had his third groin operation in nine months on Tuesday and will miss Newcastle's UEFA Cup quarter-final tie against Monaco next week.
"He's been feeling some discomfort for the last three weeks and the only thing that can be done is to operate again," club spokesman Graham Courtney said.
He said it was impossible to say when the England striker would play again although his two previous similar operations each kept him out for around a month.
England's next match is a friendly against Mexico at Wembley on March 29. Their next competitive match is a World Cup qualifier against Georgia at the end of April.
Shearer, the premier league's top scorer this season with 20 goals, had a groin operation on his left thigh last May.
He recovered sooner than expected and had an exceptional European championship last June, scoring five goals in open play for England in as many matches.
In late October he had a similar operation on his right leg and again recovered quickly, returning to the Newcastle side four weeks later.
Since then he has scored 15 goals in 18 games for Newcastle, whom he joined in July for a world record 15 million pounds ($24.5 million).
Tuesday's operation was on his right thigh.
"It's the same leg which was operated on in October, not the leg he had surgery on previously, but it's not quite as serious as in October," Courtney said.

"I think we've all recognised that Alan's not been at his best in the last few weeks even through he did score a hat-trick against Leicester (on February 2). God knows how many he would have scored if he'd have been fully fit."
